messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#98765 - prod-router-pool > router_latency_p95 > threshold (node: router-pool-12)

maya: ACK. grabbing dashboards and logs now, will post quick findings.

oliver: ACK from me too, pinging routing team. any obvious 1-off jobs?

pagerduty: oliver acknowledged the incident (via web)

maya: quick skim — spike is very short (~45-90s window) around 02:16:20 UTC. p95 hit ~980ms, p50 unaffected, error rate steady. looks like a short warmup/traffic burst rather than systemic failure.

liam: pulling deployment events — saw a canary-run at 02:16:05 that pushed ~120 reqs in 30s to router-pool-12, matches the timing.

maya: logs snippet:```
[02:16:18] router-pool-12 - evicting idle KV entries, kv-warmup=starting
[02:16:19] router-pool-12 - bundle load latency spike; queue depth briefly increased
```

maya: also ran: `kubectl top pods -l app=router -n prod --containers` — cpu on router-pool-12 spiked to 86% for one pod, then normalized.

sasha: any customer-facing errors or 5xxs?

maya: nope — 5xx rate flat. client-side latencies would maybe degrade a few requests but not broad impact. no customer pages reported.

incident-bot: Page auto-resolved at 02:18:10 UTC (duration 110s).

oliver: non-incident for now, seems noise from canary. I'm going to keep a watch for recurrence for 30m. tagging as "transient, no-customer-impact."

sasha: +1. can we add a short-term suppression for this noisy metric while we tune? or better: widen the evaluation window to 2m so single-burst doesn't fire PD.

tara: agree on tuning. small ask: create a follow-up ticket with proposed threshold/window and owner so this doesn't recur.

liam: will create a PR and a ticket. PR draft: https://git.company/redwood/infra-alerts/pulls/142 (will add screenshot & suggested 2m window change). Ticket: INF-3421.

oliver: handing off watch to liam (I need to jump to an urgent deploy). liam, pls ping if you see another flare.

liam: ack — I'll monitor dashboards for next 12h and flip suppression rule if it repeats. if we see repeat >3 within 6h we escalate.

maya: fyi I'm adding a short note in the oncall-runbook under "flapping pages" about looking for canary bursts / kv-warmup traces as first check.

oliver: thanks all. marking this as auto-resolve/no-impact in the incident tracker, closing thread unless liam reopens. :white_check_mark: 

tara: thx — small ops doc follow-up would be helpful for next week on-call.

pagerduty: Incident PD#98765 auto-resolved (closed by system).

liam: leaving watch on. will update INF-3421 after PR lands.

maya: :thumbsup:
